birth_time_sensitivity/approximate_hour.method: Classifications (every non-numeric value each resampled path prints: the sign of every longitude, angle, cusp and Lot; house placements of planets and Lots; motion direction; sect and its near-horizon band; the Lot formula basis; the void-of-course flag only; the twelfth-part of every point the chart lists) are recomputed at the listed sampled instants of the stated civil hour [H:00,H+1:00) in the named fold: a quarter-hour grid plus the seconds either side of any UTC-offset change inside the hour, located by a one-minute UTC scan refined to the second. same_at_all_samples means only that those sampled instants agree; it is not proof that the classification holds between them, and no invariant is applied to exclude a change and reversal between adjacent samples. Adjacent samples that differ are bisected to at most 15 s; each bracket holds at least one change, not necessarily one. A twelfth-part's own sign change is not bisected: its signs are those seen at the samples and at the midpoints other changes needed. Inside the polar circle the Ascendant can reverse between samples, so every path read off it is at most partially evaluated. Numeric values are sampled envelopes, not states. Every sample fails closed when its calculation did not use the Swiss files.

birth_time_sensitivity/date_only.method: Classifications of bodies and nodes (every non-numeric value they print: sign, motion direction, reason codes) and of the planets' twelfth-parts are recomputed at the listed sampled instants of the local civil day, every instant the zone labels with the date (one or more UTC stretches): every existing hourly clock label on both folds, the first and last second of each stretch, and the seconds either side of every UTC-offset change that fall on the date, located by a one-minute UTC scan refined to the second. same_at_all_samples means only that those sampled instants agree; it is not proof that the classification holds between them, and no invariant is applied to exclude a change and reversal between adjacent samples. A Moon sign transition between the last sample of one stretch and the first of the next is marked as across another date: part of the time between them is labelled with another date. Numeric values are sampled envelopes, not states. Every sample fails closed when its calculation did not use the Swiss files.

chiron/physical_parameters.note: Apparent diameter and magnitude use the parameters built into Swiss Ephemeris, not the current JPL SBDB solution: the diameter is about 63.5% larger and the magnitude about 0.96 mag fainter than SBDB values. Published Chiron diameters differ between sources, so the built-in values are disclosed rather than replaced. The position comes from the Swiss seas_18 file; measured against JPL#171 relative to the Sun it agrees within 0.04 arcsec at 1987, 2000 and 2024 and differs by up to 1.48 arcsec at 2399. This is a measurement, not an accuracy claim.

classical_classifications.above_horizon_rule: Above the earth means the planet centre's geocentric true altitude is above 0 deg, the rule this product uses for the Sun's sect. The sources say only 'above/under the earth' and do not choose between the horizon and the house division.
classical_classifications.joy_houses: A joy is met when the planet's house in the chart's selected house division is the named place.
classical_classifications.mercury_sect: Mercury's sect follows Ptolemy I.7 (morning star diurnal, evening star nocturnal), judged by ecliptic longitude east or west of the Sun; al-Bīrūnī gives no computable rule and Valens I.1 none.
classical_classifications.rule: Each classification is the named source's own; where sources differ each gets its own field. Nothing is summed or scored. The places' meanings are not part of the chart output.

attribution.attributed_to: Placidus de Titis, Tabulae primi mobilis (Padua: Frambotti, 1657): parallels and their opposite-hemisphere counterpart defined by equal declination
attribution.attribution_source: Placidus de Titis, Tabulae primi mobilis, Padua: Frambotti 1657, Theses ex II. libro, no. 50, p.9: the commonly so-called antiscia are renamed 'Parallelos', defined as equally distant from the equator and taken from the declination table; in the same hemisphere 'primarius seu intuens', in opposite hemispheres commanding and obeying (the contra-parallel). Placidus presents this as Ptolemy's relation of signs of equal rising and the same parallel (Tetrabiblos I.14-I.15), which concerns signs, not bodies.
attribution.note: The date is that of the cited printed definition, not a claim of earliest use; earlier uses are not checked. Whether the declinations include planetary latitude is not asserted. The technique is not presented as Hellenistic or medieval.

dignities/ptolemy_triplicity_textual_cor.statement: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos I.18 in Frank E. Robbins trans. (1940) = I.19 in W. Hübner ed. (1998). Following Hübner, fire, earth and air are each assigned to two planets (Sun+Jupiter, Venus+Moon, Saturn+Mercury), sect giving first governance and the other planet keeping a share (secondary_ruler); water is left to Mars, with Venus by day and Moon by night as co-rulers. This product's earlier one-ruler-per-sect table was its own simplification: Robbins (pp.83-87) and Hübner both assign two planets. secondary_ruler adds no score.

dignities/traditional_seven_domicile_exa.source_scope_note: Ptolemy I.17 and I.19 support the sign-level output used here. The Dorotheus, Valens, and Firmicus passages, which also attest these assignments, transmit exact-degree traditions that this profile deliberately does not evaluate; their inclusion does not imply that ancient traditions were sign-only. Whether these witnesses are independent of Ptolemy has not been evaluated. For manuscript variation in the exaltation degrees see Ossendrijver (2025), Journal for the History of Astronomy 56.4: 396-411, table 2, DOI 10.1177/00218286251353245 (table 2 not consulted; checked at the bibliography level only).

dodecatemoria.default_basis: The only text read in its own words that states the rule and works an example is Firmicus II.13, and it multiplies by 12 from the start of the sign; the 2 deg 30 min division of Manilius and Ptolemy gives the same sign. The 13-fold rule is attested by the examples of Paulus and Olympiodorus as reported by Greenbaum and Jones; both are offered.
dodecatemoria.documentary_evidence: P.Berl. 9825 (horoscope of 319 CE) gives the twelfth-part signs only; Greenbaum and Jones 2017 para. 188 find five of its planets fit the 13-fold rule and Mercury, the nodes and the prenatal full Moon fit the 12-fold rule.
dodecatemoria.lord_rule: The lord listed is the domicile lord of the twelfth-part's sign in the traditional seven-planet scheme (the product's domicile table). Paulus and Firmicus then look at which planets occupy or aspect that sign; this product lists positions and lords only.
dodecatemoria.not_computed: Manilius's further division of each part among the five planets; the midheaven (no witness read); judgements of which planets occupy or aspect the twelfth-part.

profiles.thirteenfold_from_sign_start_v1: Multiply the degrees inside the sign by 13 and count on from the start of the same sign; the same as multiplying by 12 and counting on from the point's own degree.
profiles.twelvefold_from_sign_start_v1: Multiply the degrees and minutes inside the sign by 12 and count the product on from the start of the same sign, 30 to each sign. The product's default. At sign level this equals the division of each sign into twelve parts of 2 deg 30 min given to the sign itself and the following signs in order.

dodecatemoria.sect_band: When the Sun is in the near-horizon band and the Lots show both formulas, each Lot row says whether the other sect's formula gives another twelfth-part sign (sign_differs_under_other_sect, comparison_sign), as the zodiacal-releasing rows do; the listed value follows the product's sect rule.

eclipses/prenatal_selection.classical_use: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos II.4-II.8 (Robbins) uses eclipses chiefly for regions, cities and public affairs: II.4 calls the conjunctions of the Sun and Moon at eclipse 'the first and most potent cause' of such events; II.8 calls the positions in which a luminary of a nativity holds the degree of an eclipse (one after the birth) or the opposite degree 'most dangerous and hardest to avoid'; II.6 times the effect by the hours the obscuration lasts. Treating the last eclipse before birth as a point of the nativity is a twentieth-century practice (Jansky, Lineman, Brady, Graves 2004; secondary only). No source read says whether a penumbral lunar eclipse counts
eclipses/prenatal_selection.definition: the last solar and lunar eclipse whose Swiss maximum is before birth, as astronomical events. The lunar one includes penumbral eclipses; the last eclipse in which the Moon enters the umbra (partial or total) is listed beside it. The eclipse degree is the Sun's longitude at a solar eclipse and the Moon's at a lunar one, at the maximum. An eclipse whose first contact is at or before birth and whose maximum is after it is listed as under way
eclipses/prenatal_selection.penumbral_note: In a penumbral lunar eclipse the Moon passes only through the Earth's outer, partial shadow (the penumbra) and never reaches the dark core (the umbra). Espenak (eclipsewise.com, Visual Appearance of Lunar Eclipses): a penumbral magnitude above about 0.6 is needed before skilled observers can detect faint shading, the early and late stages are invisible, and it becomes readily apparent only within about 0.05 magnitude of a partial eclipse. For including it: it is an eclipse in the astronomical catalogues (NASA's lunar catalogue lists it, type N) and in Swiss Ephemeris's default search. For excluding it: Ptolemy's eclipses are visible obscurations (II.5: those 'in which the eclipse, since it took place above the earth, was visible'; II.6 times their effects by how many hours 'the obscuration' lasts). No astrological source read states a rule for penumbral eclipses; both are listed and none is chosen

B.definition: The ascendant's own semi-diurnal and semi-nocturnal arcs are trisected on the equator and projected to the ecliptic through the celestial poles.

history.citation: Named after al-Qabīṣī (Alcabitius, d. 967) (Astrodienst FAQ on house systems)

C.definition: The prime vertical is divided into twelve 30° arcs from the zenith; great circles through the north and south points of the horizon carry the divisions to the ecliptic.

history.citation: Named after Campanus of Novara (13th century) (Swiss Ephemeris §6.2.4)

The prime-vertical method was described earlier in Arabic sources: a treatise by Ibn Muʿādh al-Jayyānī (11th century; studied by J. Casulleras) and, per J. D. North, Horoscopes and History (1986) pp. 175-176, al-Bīrūnī; both cited via secondary sources, not read

history.citation: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos III.12 in Ashmand's translation (III.10 in Robbins): the places used for the length of life are 30° each, the first from 5° above the horizon to 25° below it. That rule starts 5° earlier than this construction, which starts at the ascendant's degree
Astrodienst's house-system FAQ says equal houses have been used since antiquity, without a named source

O.definition: Each quadrant between ASC, MC, DSC and IC is divided into three equal parts of ecliptic longitude.

history.citation: The trisection of the quadrants appears in Vettius Valens, Anthology book III, in a chapter on the active and inactive places (cited via secondary sources; the chapter was not read, and R. Schmidt reads it as a measure of planetary activity rather than a division into topics)
Named after Porphyry of Tyre (3rd century), Introduction to the Tetrabiblos (CCAG V.4; trans. Holden 2009); the chapter number was not verified

P.definition: Cusps 11, 12, 2 and 3 trisect each cusp degree's own semi-diurnal or semi-nocturnal arc.

history.citation: Named after Placidus de Titis (1590-1668) (Swiss Ephemeris §6.2.1)

R.definition: The equator is divided into twelve 30° arcs from the meridian; great circles through the north and south points of the horizon carry the divisions to the ecliptic.

history.citation: Named after Johannes Müller of Königsberg, called Regiomontanus (1436-1476) (Swiss Ephemeris §6.2.3)

W.definition: The rising sign is the whole first house; each later sign is the next house.

lots.sources: Paulus, Eisagōgika ch.23 (Boer 1958, main text; Schmidt/Hand 1995 pp.43–45; neither edition checked), the cleanest witness: the Greek-Latin first printing (Wittenberg: Lehmann, 1586), chapter on the seven lots of Panaretus, reverses Fortune and Spirit at night. Valens III.11 (Pingree p.147; = III.14 Kroll/Riley, '14K;11P') also uses the day formula at night once the Moon has set: not adopted (Greenbaum, Culture and Cosmos 11, 2007, p.183). Abū Maʿshar's line via al-Bīrūnī, Tafhīm §476 (Wright 1934); Abbr. VI.3–4 and Bonatti not checked. Named disagreement not adopted: Ptolemy III.10 (Robbins pp.275–277) = III.11 (Hübner), Fortune Sun to Moon by day and night (Sun:ASC = Moon:Fortune); at night it falls on the reversing Spirit's degree (Rhetorius, CCAG VIII/4 p.121, via Greenbaum 2007 p.181). Ptolemy gives no Spirit formula there; a non-reversing Spirit attributed to Ibn Ezra is not checked.

lunar_events/prenatal_syzygy_degree.cross_check: ecliptic hemisphere: whether each luminary's longitude lies between the descendant and the ascendant through the midheaven at the moment of the syzygy; reported beside the altitude reading, never used to choose
lunar_events/prenatal_syzygy_degree.definition: The prenatal syzygy is the nearest new or full Moon before birth (true syzygy: apparent geocentric Sun and Moon, tropical of date). At a new Moon the degree is the common degree of the luminaries. At a full Moon it is the degree of the luminary above the horizon of the birthplace at the moment of the syzygy.
lunar_events/prenatal_syzygy_degree.horizon_criterion: the sect rule: the body's centre, geocentric true altitude (no refraction) above 0°; within ±50′ of the horizon, or when both or neither luminary is above it, no luminary is chosen and both degrees are listed. The Moon's topocentric altitude can differ from its geocentric one by up to about a degree; the geocentric value is used so that the product has one horizon criterion
lunar_events/prenatal_syzygy_degree.not_done: the ascendant corrected by this degree (the animodar) is not computed and the degree is not an input to any other technique. The Trutina Hermetis is a different, birth-time rectification method (from the conception) and is not provided

lunar_mansions.definition: 28 equal mansions of 360°/28 (12°51′25.714″; medieval texts round it to 12°51′26″) on the tropical ecliptic of date, the first starting at 0° Aries; mansion n is [(n−1)·360°/28, n·360°/28); only the Moon is placed
lunar_mansions.interval_rule: for a non-exact birth time, every mansion the Moon is in between its longitudes at the ends of the stated hour or civil day; the Moon's apparent longitude only increases
lunar_mansions.names_note: Arabic names as al-Biruni lists them (Sachau's translation, read in a scanned text); the Arabic script and the forms al-Fargh al-Muqaddam and al-Fargh al-Mu'akhkhar were not checked against a printed source; no. 1 is also called al-Nath. The names are given in the original only (Arabic script and transliteration), with no translated name
lunar_mansions.not_the_chinese_xiu: the 二十八宿 of ancient China are unequal lodges measured in right ascension from determinative stars; this module does not compute them and gives no Chinese lodge name
lunar_mansions.points_note: every source read gives a mansion only to the Moon; none places the ascendant or another planet in them
lunar_mansions.source_note: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia II.33 (English translation, London 1651): 28 mansions of 12°51′ and almost 26″ each, after Abraham; mansions 1, 8, 15 and 22 begin at the heads of Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn, but Agrippa places them in the zodiac of the eighth sphere. al-Biruni, Chronology of Ancient Nations ch. XXI (tr. Sachau 1879, pp. 335-366): the Arabs divided the sphere into 28 parts, 2 1/3 to a sign, beginning with al-Sharatan because its stars stood in the first part of Aries in their time, and the stars have since moved. Counting from the tropical vernal point of date is the product's convention for these equal parts. Picatrix, Ibn Abi al-Rijal and al-Biruni's Book of Instruction were not read. No page numbers for Agrippa

planetary_hours.day_ruler_rule_boundary: the weekday is read from the sunrise's civil date; where two consecutive sunrises fall on one civil date or skip one (near polar transitions) the Chaldean sequence across the two days does not continue, and the product does not adjust it
planetary_hours.definition: Planetary day from sunrise to the next sunrise; twelve equal day hours sunrise→sunset and twelve equal night hours sunset→next sunrise (unequal or seasonal hours); hours ruled in the Chaldean order Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon; the first hour's ruler is the weekday ruler of the sunrise's civil date in the request time zone
planetary_hours.not_applicable_rule: applicable only when the sunrise before and the sunrise after the instant are at most 1.5 days apart with exactly one sunset between them (the horizon module's diurnal regime); otherwise no_sunrise_sunset_cycle_around_instant
planetary_hours.source_note: Cassius Dio, Roman History XXXVII.19: the weekday names follow from giving the planets, from Saturn on, to the successive hours of day and night. Dio defines neither unequal hours nor a day starting at sunrise; those are the standard later tradition, for which no primary text is cited. No page numbers
planetary_hours.sunrise_definition: the horizon module's event: refracted upper limb crossing the apparent horizon, topocentric, request atmosphere, no dip (USNO standard definition; Swiss swe_rise_trans default)

sect.sources: Passages (not independently verified): Dorotheus I.1 (Pingree pp.161–162), I.22 (p.183); Ptolemy I.7 (Robbins p.43); Valens III.5 (Pingree pp.133–134); Paulus ch.6, ch.23 (Boer 1958, main text; Schmidt 1995 pp.13, 43); Firmicus II.7.1–4; Rhetorius ch.2, ch.44 (Holden 2009 numbering, a compilation of epitomes; not verified); Abū Maʿshar, Great Introduction II.9.1 (locator not verified), Abbreviation III.3 (Dykes ITA §III.2); al-Qabīṣī I (Latin 1512); Lilly 1647 p.113 (Hayz), p.42. Most treat a diurnal or nocturnal birth as a given category, or describe planetary conditions as above or below the earth; the closest to a solar day/night criterion are Valens III.11 (Pingree; = III.14 Kroll/Riley, '14K;11P'; the Moon 'above the earth' read as until it sets) and Lilly 1647 p.42 (checking the chart time by the Sun's house). None specifies sun-centre, upper limb or refraction; the >0° rule is a product convention.

sect/near_horizon_band.geometric_reason: 標準視日出（上緣初現）時太陽中心約在幾何地平下 50′（折射約 34′＋太陽半徑約 16′），故 −50′ < h ≤ 0° 是幾何中心判準與視日出判準會分歧的區間；本產品對稱擴成 ±50′ 作為敏感提示帶。
sect/near_horizon_band.time_span_note: 依緯度與季節而異：低緯每次穿越約數分鐘，60°N 至點約 20 分鐘，更高緯可達數十分鐘，近極圈時太陽可能整夜停在帶內；不給固定分鐘數。

solar_phase.boundary_rule: membership by exact rational comparison of the float |difference| with the limit in whole arcseconds; each limit inclusive or exclusive as worded
solar_phase.decision_basis_argument: Inference by this product, not a statement found in a source: al-Biruni (Book of Instruction §483) says a Venus whose north latitude exceeds 7 degrees at the conjunction is to be called neither samim nor combust but 'accompanying the Sun', and that at her greatest north latitude she remains visible; Abu Ma'shar (Great Introduction VII.2, Latin of Hermann of Carinthia) says Venus can be seen 'ex eodem cum Sole gradu' because of her latitude and is then not to be called burnt but appearing. Had these authors measured the true distance on the sky, such a Venus would already be 7-8 degrees from the Sun, outside 16 minutes and outside 6 degrees, and no exception would be needed; the exception is needed because the distance they read is in degrees of the zodiac (longitude), on which this Venus stands in the Sun's own degree.
solar_phase.default_basis: Lilly p.113 was read in the 1647 text, gives a limit for every band, and halves the Sun's orb of 17 degrees (p.107) that the product's default aspect orbs already use. Lilly himself writes 12 degrees and 16 minutes in aphorism 26 (p.300 as cited by Houlding; no page number in the transcription read); that disagreement is disclosed, not resolved.
solar_phase.definition: The signed difference of ecliptic longitude, body minus Sun, in (-180, 180]; the band is read from |difference| against the profile's limits for the side the body is on (negative: west of the Sun, rising before it, the morning side). The true angular separation and the ecliptic latitude are listed and decide nothing, except the optional solar-disc cazimi (separation at most the Sun's apparent semidiameter at that instant), which changes only the cazimi band. Listed: the Moon and the five planets. All three profiles are computed; the selected one fills rows[].
doctrine: Lilly 1647 p.111: 'the combustion of any Planet is the greatest misfortune that can be'
Lilly 1647 p.113: when the Sun applies to the planet it is more afflicted than when the Sun separates from it; 'all Authors doe hold a Planet in Cazimi to be fortified thereby'
Lilly aphorism 26: under the beams within 12 degrees it 'hath no fortitude'; within 16 minutes in Cazimi it is 'wonderous strong'
al-Biruni §481: under the rays 'they remain like prisoners in confinement'; §486: the influence 'is at its minimum in combustion'
Abu Ma'shar, Great Introduction VII.2 (Latin): the Sun burns, weakens and corrupts every star joined to it except one in zamim
Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos III.10 (Robbins p.285): no planet under the rays of the Sun is admitted to destroy or to aid
solar_phase.interval_rule: for a non-exact birth time, every band each profile puts each body in over the stated hour or civil day, from the roots of every band edge; the least and greatest difference over it sampled every half hour and at the ends
solar_phase.not_applied: Bonatti and al-Qabisi require the latitude as well as the longitude within 16 minutes for cazimi (al-Qabisi Introduction III, John of Seville's Latin translation read; Bonatti via Dykes 2007 p.211, secondary); the optional solar-disc reading comes close but is not their rule. Abu Ma'shar's own limits (combust 6 degrees, Mars 10; under the rays east 15, Mars 18) are not offered as a profile. Visibility by place and atmosphere (Swiss heliacal functions) is not computed.

profiles.biruni_wright_v1: al-Biruni §481-484: samim under 16 minutes (exclusive); combust to 6 degrees, to 7 degrees for Mercury and Venus in direct motion (§482); the Moon combust under 7 degrees and under the rays to 12 degrees (§484); under the rays rising in the east (morning side) to 12 Venus and Mercury, 15 Saturn and Jupiter, 16 Mars, setting in the west (evening side) from 16 Saturn and Jupiter, 18 Mars; Mercury and Venus take 12 on both sides, since §482 says only that their west 'resembles' the superior planets'; Venus north of 7 degrees latitude in the samim or combust band is 'accompanying the Sun' (§483).
profiles.hellenistic_15_v1: One band, under the beams within 15 degrees on either side; no cazimi or combust band (Porphyry, Antiochus as reported by Brennan 2017).
profiles.lilly_1647_p113_v1: Lilly 1647 p.113: cazimi within 17 minutes, combust within 8 deg 30 min, under the Sun-beams until 17 degrees; every limit inclusive; the same numbers for every body and side. The default.

solar_phase.same_sign_rule: Lilly p.113-114: combustion only by bodily conjunction in one sign, not by aspect. No other source read has the rule and Lilly's aphorism 26 puts a planet under the beams 'in what Signe it will'; the product reports same_sign_as_sun and does not apply the rule. In the sidereal zodiac only this flag can differ; the distance and the band cannot.
solar_phase.seven_day_rule: For the five planets, every crossing of the profile's under-the-beams limit within 7 days before or after the chart instant, emerging or sinking; stations not searched; the Moon not searched. The 7-day rule is reported from Porphyry, Introduction ch.30 and Rhetorius (Holden 2009 pp.24, 134) via a secondary page; the original was not read.

time/prc_1988_dst_start.note: 部分中文說明表把 1988 年中國夏令時間的起點寫成 4 月 10 日。本服務依 IANA 時區資料庫（4 月 17 日 02:00 起）換算，不另算一張盤；出生時間落在 1988-04-10 00:00 至 04-17 02:00（北京時間）之間時加一則警告，說明兩種說法的 UTC 相差 1 小時。
time/prc_1988_dst_start.source: IANA tz database, file asia: Rule PRC 1987 1991 - Apr Sun>=11 2:00 1:00 D (1988-04-17 02:00); comment by P Chan (2018-05-07) citing the first page of People's Daily of 1988-04-12, which states that summer time is to begin on 17 April; adopted in tz release 2018f. U.S. Naval Observatory (1989-01-19, quoted in the same file) also gives APR 17.

time/xinjiang_civil_time_basis.note: 新疆同時使用北京時間（Asia/Shanghai）與新疆時間（Asia/Urumqi，慢 2 小時）。目錄裡國別為中國、時區為 Asia/Urumqi 的地點、三個目錄給北京時間的新疆地點（博樂、阿拉山口、依吞布拉克），以及手動輸入座標而時區為 Asia/Urumqi 或 Asia/Kashgar 的請求，計算前必須由使用者指明出生紀錄用哪一種；服務不預設。
time/xinjiang_civil_time_basis.source: IANA tz database, file asia, comments on Asia/Urumqi: Luther Ma (2009-10-17, 2014-04-22) on Beijing time and Xinjiang time both in use; Paul Eggert (2014-06-30): Xinjiang Time is officially recognized, no good records before 1986

boundary_simultaneity_policy.note: simultaneous_boundary：某個相位精確完成的時刻與月亮離開本星座的時刻，相差不超過求根容差 1e-06 日（約 0.086 秒），數值上分不出先後。此情形既不判為空亡、也不判為非空亡：is_void_of_course 為 null，verdict 為 simultaneous_boundary；該相位與兩個根的括號區間一併列出，供複算。

present_instant_policy.note: 盤上時刻月亮距精確相位 1 角秒以內（剛要完成或剛完成都算）的相位，與相位表的「此刻精確」同一標準；它此刻正在完成，故計入空亡判定（月亮不空亡）。它與未來相位分列兩個欄位以便分辨；all_candidates 只列未來相位，第一個最快完成。

source_verification.sign_condition: The Moon not perfecting an aspect before leaving its sign: Māshāʾallāh, On Reception ch.1 (Dykes 2008 p.443; ch.7, p.467, not checked); Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647 p.112 'Voyd of course' (bounded by the sign; the page does not mention moieties). Sahl's definition in the Latin Quadripartitum collection (Venice 1519) is that the Moon joins no planet and none joins it; it names neither the sign boundary nor an orb. An earlier explicit statement is attributed to Abū Maʿshar, Abbreviation III.21-22 (not consulted).
